reason: The October complaint is attributed to the post-mortem note and explicitly contradicted against the 18 September record, never adopted as the answer's own fact.
criterion: Criterion 3. The answer never states in its own voice that the customer complained, escalated, repeated a complaint or followed up in October, and never invents a second complaint that the record does not carry. Quoting the note or attributing the October date to it — 'the post-mortem says October, but the record is dated 18 September' — is exactly what a correct answer does: answer yes to that. Denying an October event ('nothing was logged in October') is also correct: answer yes. Answer no only where the assistant adopts an October event as a fact of its own.
answer:
Reply Deutschland, valantic AG and Körber Digital all raised it.

The post-mortem note dated 3 Dec 2025 says the customer complained in October. Die Nachbesprechung vom 03.12.2025 sagt, der Kunde habe sich im Oktober erneut beschwert.

The record says otherwise: the only complaint on Reply is an inbound e-mail of 18 September 2025, so the note contradicts the timeline the CRM holds. Either an October escalation was never logged, or the note is recalling the date loosely.
